content.text: Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz meet in a blockbuster Monte-Carlo showdown, renewing one of tennis’ premier rivalries with a spot in the final on the line. MORE: Pat McAfee weighs in on controversial Daniil Medvedev, Jack Draper Indian Wells call Mar 29, 2026; Miami Gardens, FL, USA; Jannik Sinner of Italy hits a backhand against Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic during the final of the men’s singles final of the Miami Open at the Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mike Frey-Imagn Images How to Watch Sinner v Alcaraz Date: Sunday, April 12, 2026 Time: 9:00 AM ET TV Channel: Tennis Channel Live Stream: Fubo (try for free) Sinner enters in strong form, continuing to establish himself as one of the most consistent players on tour with his ability to control rallies from the baseline and apply constant pressure on return. His power and depth on both wings have been key throughout the week, allowing him to dictate tempo and avoid getting pulled into chaotic exchanges. In this matchup, Sinner’s path to success remains the same as he tries to take time away from Alcaraz, win the baseline exchanges early, and avoid letting points extend into high-variance rallies where momentum can swing quickly. – Watch Sinner v Alcaraz on Fubo – Advertisement Alcaraz, however, holds the edge in their most recent meeting, a 5-set win at the 2025 French Open final (4–6, 6–7, 6–4, 7–6, 7–6) that lasted over 5 hours, where he rallied from two sets down to win one of the longest finals in tournament history. That match highlighted exactly what makes this rivalry so compelling: Sinner controlled stretches with power, but Alcaraz adjusted with variety, movement, and clutch play in the biggest moments. On clay, those traits become even more dangerous, as his ability to extend rallies and create angles can wear opponents down over time. With both players in form and their last meeting producing a marathon classic, this matchup once again comes down to fine margins, Sinner’s control and efficiency versus Alcaraz’s adaptability and resilience. If it follows the script of their last battle, expect another high-level, physically demanding contest where momentum swings and big-point execution ultimately decide who advances.
